- When sentiment is consistently neutral or negative, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for 1–3 day horizons.
- After sharp price spikes, model often overshoots in subsequent days; apply a 1–3 day decay filter to smooth out overreaction.
- In low-sentiment periods, model exhibits mean reversion bias — forecast tends to be too high; adjust downward by 3–7% for 5–10 day horizons.
- If sentiment turns positive after a downtrend, model underreacts; increase forecast by 1–3% for 2–5 day horizons.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently underestimates true price volatility; add 1–2% upward bias if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- Avoid overfitting to recent history — if last 3–5 days show strong trend, model often fails to capture mean reversion; apply a 1–2 day lag correction.
